page: Amazon Web Services t4g.nano is an entry-tier, burstable general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton processor family utilizing Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance provisions 2 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is constrained to 0.5 GB of system RAM, allocating 0.25 GB per core. The processor features 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware acceleration support for AES cryptography. The instance includes no local storage and does not feature hardware GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear separation between single-thread compute efficiency and full-system throughput under constrained memory. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput reached 1507.78 points, placing it within the average tier (middle 50%), while multi-core performance scored 3000.57 points in the bottom 25% due to core count and burstable budget mechanisms. In application benchmarks, t4g.nano delivered 2.34 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.45 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, reflecting baseline operational constraints in throughput-heavy scenarios.

The primary operational tradeoff of t4g.nano centers on its 0.5 GB RAM footprint, which severely limits memory-intensive execution runtimes. However, its ARM-based architecture yields high compute efficiency per unit of resource allocation for lightweight workloads. The instance is suited for low-traffic microservices, lightweight monitoring agents, headless cron runners, simple proxy gateways, and non-demanding development environments with minimal memory requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.nano is a micro-tier burstable virtual machine powered by AWS Graviton ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 2 vCPUs clocked at 2.5 GHz along with 0.5 GB of system memory, yielding 0.25 GB per core without simultaneous multithreading. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show solid per-core computational capabilities, achieving an average-tier stress-ng single-core score of 1507.78, while multi-core throughput registers at 3000.57 points due to burstable allocation limits. Redis throughput reaches 2.34 million operations per second, alongside 2.45 GB/sec for static web delivery. Because of its constrained memory profile and zero baseline network bandwidth, t4g.nano is specifically suited for low-overhead administrative utilities, basic proxies, edge telemetry agents, and lightweight background cron tasks that operate within tight memory bounds.
